title: Tiered Huffman + Variable-bit KV compression probe (FP8/INT8/INT4) and quality-policy sweep
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Summary:
This ticket runs an exploratory set of experiments for a tiered KV compression strategy that combines entropy-aware variable-length encoding (Huffman-style packing) with per-layer adaptive bitwidth quantization (FP8 / INT8 / INT4) and a lightweight lossy predictor for small-value smoothing. The goal is to reduce GPU KV cache memory pressure in long-context workloads (8k-64k) while keeping generative quality and latency within product SLOs. We explicitly probe interactions with continuous batching: variable request sequence lengths and varying prefix reuse degrade packing efficiency and can increase CPU overhead for unpacking.

Hypothesis:
1) Entropy-aware packing applied after per-row quantization will give 10-30% additional memory reduction compared to uniform per-row int8 quantization for real prompt distributions.
2) Per-layer sensitivity: early layers (close to embeddings) are more sensitive to INT4; later layers tolerate FP8/INT8 with negligible logprob drift. A small per-layer metadata store (2-4 bits per row) for bitwidth and packing offsets is acceptable.
3) Continuous batching pressure is the primary operational risk: unpacking latency and variability may increase tail latencies for small requests unless we implement a fast path that caches decompressed hot prefixes.

Experiment plan and matrix:
- Models: open-model-compat 70B transformer (server build used in runtime: rwinf/70b-2026-02-20), and a 13B surrogate for faster sweeps.
- Hardware: A100 80GB (hosted) and H100-80GB (dedicated) nodes.
- Workloads: 3 synthetic mixes derived from production traces:
  * "chat-short": avg prefix 64 tokens, high reuse, PLG chat agents.
  * "search-long": avg prefix 4k tokens, low reuse, retrieval-augmented generation.
  * "docs-stream": avg prefix 24k tokens, append-only, continuous batching heavy.
- Compression variants (each combined with per-layer policy):
  1) baseline: FP16 no compression
  2) int8-uniform: per-row static INT8
  3) int4-layerwise: per-layer INT4 or INT8 decision using sensitivity probe
  4) fp8-mantissa-reduction: bfloat-like FP8 profile tuned for kv-range
  5) hybrid-huffman: quantize (INT4/INT8/FP8) then entropy-pack using variable-length blocks (Huffman-like), with 64B alignment for GPU coalescing
  6) tiered-hot-cold: store hot prefixes as native FP16, cold prefixes compressed with hybrid-huffman
- Metrics:
  * Memory reduction: measured KV bytes on-device per concurrent request mix
  * Per-token latency and P99 latency under continuous batching
  * Quality: delta in average token logprob, normalized perplexity, and generation-level embedding cosine similarity (SimHash on last 128 tokens) vs baseline
  * Downstream QA score: automated eval on a 2k prompt QA set (exact-match and F1)
  * Failure modes: decoding stalls, hallucinations flagged in heuristic detector, gradient of output drift over long prefix streams
- Data collection: 100k requests per variant from trace-sampled inputs; 10 full-generation human-review buckets for drift artifacts

Implementation notes:
- Prototype uses a GPU-side unpack kernel (CUDA) that can decode a packed block into a staging buffer; packing is done on the CPU path before issuing batched KV writes to GPU in the dedicated experiments. For hosted CPU-limited paths we test a GPU-assisted streaming decompressor.
- Per-row metadata encoded in a compact table (bitfields): 2 bits for bitwidth hint, 1 bit for hot/cold, 5 bits for run-length of identical rows (helps packing). Metadata stored separately in CSR-like form to avoid per-KV-pointer overhead.
- To mitigate continuous-batching jitter we added a small LRU for decompressed prefix blocks; experiments measure hit-rate and effect on latency distribution.

Preliminary results (short-run, 70B model on A100):
- memory: hybrid-huffman + tiered-hot-cold reduced KV bytes by 41% vs baseline FP16 and by 22% vs uniform INT8.
- perf: average throughput increased ~12% for long-context workloads due to more cacheable KV in GPU memory; P99 latency regressed by ~18% for chat-short without decompression cache enabled (unpacking spike), but recovered to +2% with decompression LRU enabled.
- quality: average token logprob delta for hybrid-huffman was -0.015 nats/token (small but measurable); normalized perplexity increased 2.3% overall. QA exact-match drop was 1.1 points absolute on the 2k set. For per-layer INT4 on first 4 layers, perplexity jumped 9% and QA drop 6.8 points --- confirming layer sensitivity.
- human eval: in 10 sampled long generations, 2 showed mild factual drift attributable to quantization noise in high-entropy tokens (dates/names).

Trade-offs and decisions:
- Acceptable production envelope: hybrid-huffman with per-layer policy that avoids INT4 in first 6 layers, and marks top-2 rows per KV as "hot" to remain in native FP16. This yields ~30% memory reduction with <2.5% normalized perplexity increase and <1.5 points QA drop.
- Operational control: expose a per-customer memory-vs-quality knob in the Console (low/medium/high compression) that maps to the policy; require rollout to Dedicated first and gating by runtime-1.22 release flags.
- Risk mitigation: decompression LRU must be enabled on hosted endpoints and tuned to keep P99 < 300ms for chat-short; fallback to uniform INT8 if the runtime detects repeated unpacking spikes.

- [ ] Full sweep across H100 nodes and 70B baseline; collect 1M requests per variant for statistical significance (Asha).
- [ ] Design Console knob mapping and feature flag for early access (PM: Lina Zhou). Link to Confluence planning doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/KV/kv-tiered-compression-probe
- [ ] Run adversarial prompts (dates/IDs/names) and augment heuristic detector to flag high-entropy content requiring conservative policy (Security & Safety sync).
- [ ] Draft runtime-1.22 release notes for Dedicated customers and include rollback policies.
